_note: Removing a parameter's sentence from a compact description (Agent readOnly/isolation/SendMessage, Build directory, Typecheck baseline, RunTests framework, Grep's symbols mode) leaves the test green by design: the schema still names and describes the parameter, and schema text counts as something the model reads. Only behaviors the schema does not state are probed here.

probes.replace: a .diff/.patch by file, with symbol='<path>' for one file's hunks), symbol='X'

probes.name: Read ignores the compact switch
compact Grep stops describing the broad-search pivot
probes.find: A broad "content" search comes back as the "symbols" map; pass \`head_limit\`, or narrow \`path\`/\`glob\`, to get the lines.

probes.name: compact apply_patch drops the End of File anchor
probes.find: ; "*** End of File" anchors a hunk to the end of the file. The "@@" line is a search cursor
probes.replace: . The "@@" line is a search cursor

probes.name: compact Agent drops the fork semantics
probes.find: - Omitting \`subagent_type\` forks you: the child inherits this whole conversation and re-reads it on every call it makes, so a fork costs more the deeper the session. A fresh agent (\`subagent_type: "Code"\` or a named one) starts from your prompt alone. Default to a fresh agent; fork only when the child needs what is in this conversation and a paragraph cannot carry it. Don't set \`model\` on a fork.
